_README: Pins a specific visitor to a specific level's Office Hours stage,
overriding the normal pick. Same idea, and same file shape, as
level_opponent_overrides.json — a separate file rather than widening that
one, so a mistake in this newer mechanic can't touch the well-tested
opponent one.
WRITTEN BY HAND, like rules.json and booster_standing.json.
export_data.py never overwrites it — Cameron edits this file directly.
WHY THIS EXISTS. A Non-combat (Office Hours) stage's visitors are picked
the same dynamic way opponents are: every visitor whose Visitors-tab
'stages' list names that STxx is eligible, and the game draws however
many the stage's own 'Opponent Count' range calls for (see BattleSetup.gd,
_visitors_for()) — the same range column combat stages use for opponents,
not a separate one. That default is DYNAMIC on purpose, same as the
opponent pick. Sometimes a level needs a NAMED visitor regardless of who
else is eligible. That is what this file is for.
HOW TO USE IT. Add one object per pin to the 'overrides' list:
level_id     the level, e.g. "LV11"
slot         which Stage ID column on that level's row, 1-10, matching
stage_1 .. stage_10 on the Levels tab
visitor_id   the visitor to use, from visitors.json — must be one whose
own 'stages' list already includes the STxx in that slot,
or the game logs a warning and falls back to the dynamic
pick rather than seating someone in a room they are not
written to be eligible for
A pin fills one of the drawn slots; if the stage's Opponent Count calls
for more than one visitor, the rest are still the dynamic pick.
Nothing is in here yet. Every level currently uses the dynamic pick.
